summary: CyberPowerPC listed prebuilt gaming PCs equipped with NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Founders Edition GPUs on Walmart as part of the retailer's NVIDIA GeForce promotion this week; the RTX 5080 configurations ($2,299 with a Ryzen 9800X3D and $2,399 with an Intel Core Ultra 9 285K) sold out within about a day, with Walmart reportedly moving over 1,000 units, while the two RTX 5070 systems ($1,599 with a Ryzen 7800X3D and $1,549 with an Intel 14700KF) remained in stock.
quote: CyberPowerPC listed prebuilt PCs with NVIDIA RTX 5080 and 5070 Founders Edition GPUs at Walmart, but the RTX 5080 rigs sold out very quickly - in just a day, in fact (with over 1,000 units moved). Two RTX 5070 PCs remain available at $1,599 and $1,549. … VideoCardz reports that the manufacturer of prebuilts is selling PCs with Founders Edition RTX 5080 and 5070 GPUs inside them via Walmart , as part of the retailer's NVIDIA GeForce promotion this week. … According to VideoCardz, the cheaper RTX 5080 systems sold out in a day flat, with Walmart shifting over 1,000 units apparently.

summary: TweakTown reported that third-party NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 graphics cards were selling for around $850 in the US, up from around $650 a couple of months earlier, with GPU pricing worsening because of a memory (RAM) shortage; it said standalone third-party RTX 5080 cards now start at about $1,500 in the US.
quote: I expect the RTX 5070 PCs will last longer - they're both still in stock at the time of writing - but even these represent a decent bargain given that you're looking at around $850 for a third-party card in the US these days. That's up from around $650 just a couple of months ago, and GPU pricing is getting a whole lot worse thanks to the RAM crisis. … It's hardly surprising that the RTX 5080 PCs flew off the shelves at Walmart, given that the standalone graphics card now costs from $1,500 upwards in the US.

reported_by: Sakeena Fiza, NVIDIA validation engineer, in an NVIDIA Blog post
summary: NVIDIA validation engineer Sakeena Fiza, writing in an NVIDIA corporate blog post, said she saw the NVIDIA Rubin GPU working at system level for the first time in the company's data center systems engineering lab, the first time a Rubin GPU has enumerated at system level; she describes validation as work done on a device before mass production begins and before customers depend on it. The item gives no date for the milestone, no quantities, no shipment or production timing and no customer or revenue detail.
quote: One of Fiza’s earliest and most enduring memories of working at NVIDIA is the collective joy she experienced when she saw the NVIDIA Rubin GPU working for the first time at a system level. … “It literally just said, ‘NVIDIA Corporation Device,’” she recalls. “And everyone’s cheering and celebrating because it’s the first time in the world that a Rubin GPU enumerated at a system level.” … Fiza describes validation — the process of ensuring a physical device works correctly before mass production begins — as becoming “the first customers for the product,” exercising hardware to its limits in a range of real-world conditions before anyone else has to depend on it.

said_by: Sea Group (Li Kuangli, senior director of partnerships and strategy) and Nvidia
summary: At Nvidia AI Day Singapore, Sea Group senior director of partnerships and strategy Li Kuangli said Sea Group will be the first enterprise in Southeast Asia to adopt Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform (Nvidia's Vera CPU combined with Rubin GPUs), as part of an AI strategy in which Sea runs every layer of its technology stack except the chips. The companies said Vera Rubin will allow Sea to build and deploy AI models and agents at a larger scale, but did not say how large the deployment will be or when it will go live.
quote: Sea Group will be the first enterprise in Southeast Asia to adopt Nvidia’s Vera Rubin platform , building on an artificial intelligence (AI) strategy that lets it run every layer of its technology stack except the chips. … The companies said Vera Rubin, which combines Nvidia’s Vera central processing unit (CPU) with its Rubin graphics processing units (GPUs), will allow Sea to build and deploy AI models and agents at a larger scale. They did not say how big the deployment will be, or when it will go live.

summary: Sea Group senior director of partnerships and strategy Li Kuangli disclosed that Sea runs its own datacentre infrastructure of over 150,000 servers and more than 25,000 GPUs across 40-plus datacentres worldwide, with a combined critical IT load in excess of 100MW; the network has more than 120 interconnections with tier-one internet service providers and handles over 1.1 exabytes of traffic a month (about 700 million hours of high-definition video, by Li's calculation).
quote: On top of the chips is infrastructure that Sea runs itself: over 150,000 servers and more than 25,000 GPUs across 40-plus datacentres worldwide, with a combined critical IT load in excess of 100MW. The network has more than 120 interconnections with tier-one internet service providers, and handles over 1.1 exabytes of traffic a month – about 700 million hours of high-definition video, by Li’s calculations.

summary: William Tjhi, head of applied research at AI Singapore (AISG), said AISG — creator of the Sea-Lion family of open models for Southeast Asian languages — is expanding Sea-Lion with Nvidia's Nemotron open models and NeMo tools.
quote: AISG, creator of the Sea-Lion family of open models for Southeast Asian languages, is expanding it with Nvidia’s Nemotron open models and NeMo tools.

summary: Nvidia vice-president of solutions architecture and engineering Marc Hamilton, speaking at Nvidia AI Day Singapore, showed GitHub data in which new repositories had climbed to 20 million a month by April, which he attributed to growing use of coding agents; he said such agents can run thousands of inferences on a single task and that some AI-native companies burnt through their annual coding budgets in the first month or two of this year.
quote: Marc Hamilton, vice-president of solutions architecture and engineering at Nvidia, showed GitHub data in which new repositories had climbed to 20 million a month by April, which he attributed to the growing use of coding agents . Those agents can run thousands of inferences on a single task, and some AI-native companies burnt through their annual coding budgets in the first month or two of this year, he said.

reported_by: Andriy Myronenko, Supriya V. Thathachary and Monty Zarrouk (NVIDIA Technical Blog)
summary: NVIDIA announced on its developer blog the open release of NV-Reason-CT, a vision-language model purpose-built for 3D CT analysis that combines a full 3D vision transformer encoder with a Qwen3.5-4B language model to generate radiologist-style chain-of-thought reasoning and structured reports; NVIDIA says the model is now openly available for research and development, with weights on Hugging Face and code on GitHub. NVIDIA describes it as an open research and development foundation, not an autonomous diagnostic system or a cleared clinical product, and reports state-of-the-art CT-RATE benchmark results (Macro-F1 0.614, Macro-AUROC 0.871) versus published 3D contrastive and fused 2D/3D baselines. No revenue, pricing, customer order or capacity commitment is attached to the release.
quote: NV-Reason-CXR reasoning methodology extends to 3D CT analysis with NV-Reason-CT, a vision language model purpose-built for volumetric imaging. … NV-Reason-CT is an open research and development foundation; not an autonomous diagnostic system or a cleared clinical product. It is an AI foundation model designed for researchers and developers building specialized CT analysis applications to post-train for their use case. … NV-Reason-CT achieves state-of-the-art results on the CT-RATE benchmark with a Macro-F1 of 0.614 and Macro-AUROC of 0.871, outperforming published 3D contrastive and fused 2D/3D baselines. … Ready to get started? The model is now openly available for research and development.

summary: IonQ announced on 23 September 2026 that it will make the first on-premise quantum computing deployment at NVIDIA's Accelerated Quantum Research Center (NVAQC): an IonQ Superion 256 system will be installed at the facility and directly linked to an NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 system via NVIDIA NVQLink, with workloads orchestrated by the open NVIDIA CUDA-Q platform, under a joint research program on hybrid software development and large-scale system prototyping. IonQ said installation at NVAQC is scheduled for next year (2027).
quote: Today, IonQ (NYSE: IONQ) announced that it will be the first on-premise quantum computing deployment at the NVIDIA Accelerated Quantum Research Center (NVAQC). … As part of the partnership, an IonQ Superion 256 system will be installed at the NVAQC and directly linked with an NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 system via NVIDIA NVQLink , with workloads orchestrated by the open NVIDIA CUDA-Q platform. … The joint research program will focus on hybrid software development and large-scale system prototyping, generating open results and a guide for future AI use cases and quantum-GPU co-design. … Installation at NVAQC is scheduled for next year.

summary: Nvidia told shareholders in May 2026 that it would raise its quarterly dividend to $0.25 per share from $0.01 per share, an increase the Morningstar author calculates at 2,400%. The author estimates roughly $25 billion per year would be returned to shareholders through the dividend, which would make Nvidia one of the largest dividend payers in the US market; that annual figure is the author's approximation, not a company-disclosed total.
quote: In May, Nvidia told shareholders that it would increase its quarterly payout to $0.25 per share from $0.01 per share. That’s a 2,400% increase, according to my calculations! … But in absolute terms, Nvidia’s dividend is huge. Something like $25 billion per year will be returned to shareholders. That sum will make Nvidia one of the largest dividend payers in the US stock market.

summary: Nvidia announced an $80 billion share buyback program at the time of its May 2026 dividend declaration, per the Morningstar article.

summary: NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang is scheduled to attend President Donald Trump's state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping on Sept. 24, 2026, along with other technology leaders, as the U.S. and China discuss AI, trade, tariffs and advanced semiconductors. The article says the dinner itself does not guarantee policy changes but could provide a backdrop for signals on NVIDIA's access to the Chinese market and export restrictions.
quote: Nvidia (NVDA) investors have a key date to watch as CEO Jensen Huang is set to attend President Donald Trump's state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping on Sept. 24, along with other prominent technology leaders at the White House. The high-profile gathering comes as the U.S. and China navigate sensitive issues involving artificial intelligence (AI), trade, tariffs, and advanced semiconductor technology. … Huang's presence is particularly notable for Nvidia, given the company's position at the center of the global AI chip market and the ongoing U.S.-China technology relationship. Investors will be watching whether discussions around AI and semiconductor trade create any signals relevant to Nvidia's access to the Chinese market, export restrictions, or the broader outlook for AI infrastructure demand. … While the dinner itself does not guarantee any policy changes, Sept. 24 could provide an important backdrop for Nvidia stock as the market weighs the potential implications of renewed U.S.-China engagement.

summary: NVIDIA reported fiscal second-quarter 2027 results on Aug. 26, 2026, for the quarter ended July 26: revenue rose 106% year over year to a record $96.2 billion (up 18% sequentially) and exceeded prior guidance of $91 billion plus or minus 2%. Non-GAAP net income rose 118% to $54 billion, adjusted EPS rose 120% to $2.22, non-GAAP gross margin rose to 75% from 72.5%, and operating income rose 124% to $63.7 billion. Data Center revenue was $89 billion, up 117% year over year and the majority of total revenue.
quote: Nvidia delivered another blockbuster quarter, reporting its fiscal second-quarter 2027 results on Aug. 26, for the quarter ended July 26. Revenue reached a record $96.2 billion, up 106% year-over-year (YoY) from $46.7 billion, and increased 18% sequentially. The result also comfortably exceeded Nvidia's prior guidance of $91 billion, plus or minus 2%. … The company's profitability expanded even faster. On a non-GAAP basis, net income climbed 118% to $54 billion, versus $24.8 billion in Q2 fiscal 2026, while adjusted EPS jumped 120% to $2.22, exceeding expectations. Non-GAAP gross margin rose to 75% from 72.5%. Operating income surged 124% YoY to $63.7 billion. … Nvidia's Data Center segment remained the primary growth engine, generating $89 billion in revenue, up 117% YoY from the prior-year quarter and representing the majority of total company revenue. The performance reflects continued demand for Nvidia's accelerated-computing platforms as hyperscalers and AI companies expand infrastructure.

summary: NVIDIA guided fiscal third-quarter 2027 revenue to $108 billion, plus or minus 2%, and GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins to approximately 74%, plus or minus 50 basis points. The forecast assumes no Data Center compute revenue from China.

summary: Street analysts expect NVIDIA's EPS to grow 102.4% year over year to $9.25 in fiscal 2027, followed by another 65.7% increase to $15.33 in fiscal 2028, according to the article's consensus forecast.

summary: AI cloud provider Nscale filed for a U.S. initial public offering on 18 September 2026 disclosing that it lost $1.02 billion in the first six months of 2026 on revenue of just $140.6 million — the financial condition of the counterparty to which NVIDIA is committing $1 billion of convertible financing.

summary: NVIDIA is committing $1 billion to a $3.1 billion convertible financing for AI cloud provider Nscale, the IPO candidate whose filing the article discusses; the article notes this gives NVIDIA direct capital exposure in addition to its role as hardware supplier.
quote: Yet NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ: NVDA ) is committing $1 billion to a $3.1 billion convertible financing, while Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ: MSFT ) is expected to become one of Nscale's most important customers. … Nvidia can still benefit from Nscale's expansion by selling the picks and shovels, although its $1 billion financing commitment gives it direct capital exposure as well.

summary: Nscale disclosed that as of 31 August 2026 it had $103.4 billion of active and contracted total contract value under long-term take-or-pay contracts with a weighted-average contract life of about 5.7 years, operating in 14 regions with more than 10 gigawatts of potential power capacity — the contracted demand base underlying the Nscale build-out NVIDIA supplies and is financing.
quote: As of August 31, Nscale had $103.4 billion of active and contracted total contract value under long-term take-or-pay contracts, with a weighted-average contract life of about 5.7 years. It operates in 14 regions and has more than 10 gigawatts of potential power capacity.
